cells.tense: The ground for deciding is here, solid enough to stand on now.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Pick a direction you're about to settle on, ask someone it touches what it's like for them, and sit with their answer for a minute without steering it. Then decide.
cells.core:
You can put weight behind one direction and stay with it — the building kind of decision, the one that gets used and holds. The ground is steady enough for that. A person says one thing and your answer is already there; the shape under it has been setting a while.

Here is the way in. Before you fix on a direction, ask someone it touches what it's like for them. Then sit with their answer a minute. Don't correct it, don't explain why you've already decided; let it stand without being steered. The odd part is that deciding gets steadier after, not weaker — you're standing on both what you hold and where they stand. A decision made with their answer still in earshot is firmer, not softer.
cells.sheetLine: You can decide here, and the decision holds through long use.
cells.verb: Building something that holds through long use

cells.tense: A future is being forced open ahead of any ground that could carry it.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Take one feeling you've already judged in this direction — the push or the guilt — and make the honest call on it yourself: what holding the direction gives them, what it takes.
cells.core:
The direction is already decided and the building starts before the ground is ready. You say this way, and you've already forced it — the next five moves and the objections, all held against a future nobody can set a stone in. What was strength is now driving ahead of what deciding can carry. The weight presses down on whoever the direction touches, and they're carrying a plan they didn't get to weigh.

One move breaks that loop. Take one feeling sitting in this direction — the push you feel, or the guilt under it — and judge it fairly yourself. Not the whole situation; one feeling. What does holding this direction give them, and what does it take? Say the honest verdict out loud, then let the direction stand on what's left. Decide with the verdict in hand, not before it.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing a direction the ground can't carry yet.
cells.verb: Building something that holds through long use

cells.tense: You stand at a threshold the rest of you already crossed.
cells.act: drop one condition you set and take the step
cells.ask: Find the hidden price you've put on committing here — the perfect moment, or knowing it'll work. Name it, set it aside, and commit without it.
cells.core:
The direction exists and can't be picked. You've stood at the threshold while the rest of you crossed — repeating the case for each path, keeping every one open. The decision was there; it isn't coming forward. This isn't quite indecision. It's holding the starting gun back. Nothing you build in here begins.

Release does the deciding. There's a price you've set on committing, and underneath it a wish for a guarantee, not a reason. The one about the perfect time, or the one about knowing it will work. Name it and set it aside. Then decide — no better information needed. A first step falls into one direction, and the next one appears after it, not before. That is how moving works here; the hesitation was the only thing keeping it open.
cells.sheetLine: You've kept every direction open and moved in none of them.
cells.verb: Building something that holds through long use

cells.tense: The direction is chosen and steered every day while the one steering looks away.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin a small thing in this direction with nothing riding on it and no plan past the first move — started only because starting is what you like doing.
cells.core:
The direction is chosen constantly and gets described as friction. The call is yours, and if someone summarized what you've told them, the deciding circle would be empty. You speak of your choices as if they were conditions you found — where circumstances pushed, where the options narrowed. The direction is yours. That fact got parked with a story anyone would accept.

What was yours first was starting things. Begin one thing in this direction before you know where it ends — small, alive, nothing riding on it — because the starting is where you feel most yourself. Not as an obligation; an experiment. Before the deciding was for anyone else, it was a spark. Light one in the open, and the direction shows who set it. Your hands were on the wheel the whole time, with a driver who wasn't looking.
cells.sheetLine: You choose the direction daily and say the road chose for you.
cells.verb: Building something that holds through long use

attempts.check: The medicine's own word 'holding' invites a claim the record does not make — that the person is finally settled; drop it and stay with the bare knowing of which way to move. A reader could object that picking one direction is not a feeling-connection act at all, so the ask is framed as connection done through the choosing, not instead of it. The ask survives being wrong: staying with the answer for a minute trains the choosing either way, and even a misread leaves a usable move in the same seat. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'you can build in the dark' — it flatters the card's picture and does no work here.
